record.name: Potrero Power Station Block 15 / Station A
record.summary: Adaptive reuse of the 1901-02 Station A turbine hall into an 11-story, ~456,000 gsf office building with an eight-story vertical addition, approved by the Planning Commission October 22, 2020; as of the 2024 annual compliance report, no construction had started.

notes.accuracy_caveat: APPROXIMATE -- this block is not yet built and does not correspond to any subdivided Assessor parcel: it currently sits on vacant/graded land within the former power station site (unaddressed in DataSF's Assessor roll). Traced from an adopted regulatory diagram via multi-point real-street georeferencing (see digitization_method), but this diagram is dated 2020 and may not reflect later design changes (as already found for the UCSF/Sophie Maxwell area -- see digitization_method). Treat vertex positions as accurate to roughly 10-25m, not survey-grade, and treat the block's applicability itself as somewhat more provisional than Mission Rock's or Pier 70's equivalent entries. Rebuilt 2026-09-16 via GDAL GCP/TPS georeferencing -- see digitization_method. Re-measured 2026-09-16 (third pass) in a single consistent pixel-detection pass across the whole block layout -- see digitization_method. Re-corrected 2026-09-16 (fourth pass) after fixing a mis-measured GCP -- see digitization_method.
notes.digitized_from: Potrero Power Station Design for Development, Figure 6.2.3 - Building Height Plan (p.245).
notes.why_no_real_parcel: A real Assessor parcel may exist under this block (part of the site's larger, largely unaddressed footprint), but it has not been subdivided per the masterplan's individual named blocks -- this uses hand-traced approximate geometry instead.
notes.regulatory_context: Station A: the site's historic 1901 unreinforced-brick turbine hall, standing vacant/unused. Adaptive reuse into ~403,750 GSF office/R&D (plus 16,225 sf of terraces and a public 'Turbine Hall'/mid-block passage to Power Station Park) via 8 new floors built above the retained historic shell, designed by Herzog & de Meuron with Adamson Associates, approved by the SF Planning Commission Oct 22, 2020 -- all confirmed directly against the actual Planning Commission approval packet. Max height 205 ft (historic base + addition). Construction had NOT started as of an August 2025 source -- the site's flagship preservation project, reversing an original demolition plan after Historic Preservation Commission/SF Heritage advocacy.

facts.value: Herzog & de Meuron, with Adamson Associates, Inc.

205 ft total (existing base plus 8-story addition); a 145-foot and 160-foot building height maximum is described elsewhere in the same memo as the 'prevailing' limits subject to a 15% exterior-volume reduction for mass above the Station A walls, and the D4D's Figure 6.2.3 shows Block 15 with an upper-height callout of 230 ft on part of the block
approximately 403,750 sq ft of office use plus 52,410 sq ft exempt from gross floor area calculations, for approximately 456,120 GSF total
existing Station A plus an 8-story vertical addition, described elsewhere as resulting in an 11-story building overall
76 Class 1 and 10 Class 2 bicycle parking spaces, 4 showers, 24 lockers, 2 off-street loading spaces via a new 33-ft entrance on Georgia Lane
Individually eligible for the California Register of Historical Resources under Criterion 1 (Events); contributor to the Third Street Industrial District
office (D4D final Table 3.1.1 marks Residential and Hotel Not Permitted on Block 15; Non-Retail Sales/Services, Laboratory and Life Science uses are permitted)
Plant Construction (per the project's MEP engineer, Meyers+)
Project (Blocks 11, 12 and 15) is seeking LEED Gold certification; all three are designed as all-electric buildings

open_questions: No construction-start date is stated in any source found; the most recent primary source found (the 2024 annual compliance report, submitted March 2025) describes only design approval and does not report construction underway on Station A.

The D4D's Figure 6.2.3 shows a 230-ft upper-height callout for part of Block 15, while the 2022 design review approval describes a 205-ft total height and references '145-foot and 160-foot' prevailing maximums for the vertical addition; these figures are not reconciled here.

The Chronicle's July 2026 report of a proposed +30 ft height increase for Station A is tied to a Development Agreement amendment (BOS File 260724 / Planning Code ordinance File 260770) that was still pending Board of Supervisors action as of this dossier's last-verified date; it is recorded here as an expected/proposed change, not an adopted one.
No source found stating a cost estimate for Station A's rehabilitation and vertical addition.

The hosted image (potrero_block15_station_a_deir_2018.jpg) is kind: before, but it is not a single photograph -- it is a composite DEIR report page carrying six separate existing-conditions photos of Station A's turbine hall and machine shop, each with its own caption. Flagging in case a document-style kind fits it better than a single before photo.

The newly added now photo is dated 2020-02-17; labeled now rather than before because the most recent primary source found (the 2024 annual compliance report, submitted March 2025) still describes no construction activity on Station A beyond design approval, so the building's exterior likely hasn't changed since. If construction has started since this dossier's last_verified date, this photo is out of date and should be revisited.
